methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $80M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
CarbonCapture Inc., a Series B climate and energy company founded by Adrian Corless, has raised $80M to date. The valuation analysis references a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (LNZA), with particular focus on three same-sector, adjacent-stage peers: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C).

Two valuation methods triangulate to a defensible range. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $152M from the $80M raised proxy. The peer-median approach anchors to the $1.0B median valuation across the three comparable companies, reflecting the upper-stage positioning and capital intensity of the climate-tech sector. This method implies $1.0B as a reference point, though the peer range spans $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $129M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $576M. The wide dispersion—reflecting uncertainty in stage-to-stage progression and peer applicability—warrants scrutiny of CarbonCapture's technology differentiation, path to revenue, and capital efficiency relative to the comparison set. The stage-progression floor of $152M and peer-median ceiling of $1.0B represent the key method anchors. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage discount to Series C comparables and whether CarbonCapture's business model commands peer-equivalent multiples.
